candidates.access_status: open web; application served from apl.cnb.cz / jerrs.cnb.cz
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Prefer the WS JERRS web services and the ČNB open-data endpoints over scraping the Oracle-APEX-style web UI. Snapshot the bank and foreign-branch lists monthly and diff against the prior run to detect entry/exit/renaming events. Cross-check with the National Open Data Catalogue dataset 'Seznam bank a poboček zahraničních bank působících na území České republiky'.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs-language regulator-registry query, snowballed to the web-services and open-data pages and to the national open-data catalogue entry
queries_used: ČNB seznam regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů JERRS vyhledávání banky
ČNB seznam poboček bank z členského státu EU působících v ČR mBank Hello bank přehled

candidates.source_name: or.justice.cz – Veřejný rejstřík a Sbírka listin (commercial register collection of deeds)
candidates.why_relevant: The legal backstop for every unlisted bank in this cell. Czech law requires accounting entities in the public register to deposit annual financial statements and annual reports in the Sbírka listin, free to access without registration, as downloadable PDFs. This catches filings that a bank has quietly dropped from its own website, provides the audited statutory version rather than the marketing 'graphic' edition, and supplies board/ownership changes and merger deeds — exactly what is needed to date events like the Max banka absorption into Banka CREDITAS. Also the only route to documents for entities that publish nothing voluntarily.
candidates.source_subtype: national company register / statutory document repository
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Resolve each bank's IČO first (via ARES or JERRS), then pull its Sbírka listin document list and download new filings. ARES (ares.cz) offers a cleaner API-style lookup for the IČO step. Run annually after the statutory filing season, plus ad hoc when a merger or licence change is suspected.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles reasoning about who is legally compelled to archive corporate filings, then cs-language query to confirm the portal and its scope
queries_used: justice.cz sbírka listin výroční zpráva banka or.justice.cz veřejný rejstřík účetní závěrka

candidates.source_name: ČNB – ARAD time series, supervisory statistics & payment-system statistics
candidates.why_relevant: ARAD is the regulator's public time-series database, and ČNB explicitly publishes selected supervisory statistics through it (entity counts and basic financial statements under 'Basic Financial Market Indicators') alongside harmonised, non-confidential payment statistics. For a source-scouting pass this matters because it supplies the sector denominator against which any individual second-tier bank's disclosed numbers can be normalised, and it covers payment-instrument and channel aggregates that individual challenger banks never break out. Machine-friendly time series, so it is a genuinely low-cost long-term collection target.
candidates.access_status: open web; SPA application at cnb.cz/arad
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the ARAD application (https://www.cnb.cz/arad/#/cs/home) to identify the relevant series ids for supervisory and payment statistics, then pull on a fixed schedule; the app is a single-page application so a plain HTML crawler will not work — target its data endpoints or the published dataset exports.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs-language statistical query following first-principles reasoning about who aggregates bank-level regulatory returns
queries_used: ČNB ARAD databáze časové řady banky počet poboček bankomatů platební styk statistika
local_language_terms_used: informační povinnosti banky a pobočky zahraniční banky

candidates.source_name: Česká bankovní asociace – ČBA Online & ČBA Monitor (sector statistics, Hypomonitor, expert outputs)
candidates.why_relevant: The industry association aggregates 'basic indicators on the development of the domestic banking sector' explicitly built from ČNB statistics plus the mandatory published data of individual banks — i.e. it does part of the cross-bank normalisation work for this cell already, including for the smaller banks whose figures are otherwise scattered across ad hoc XLSX annexes. It also runs ČBA Hypomonitor (mortgage market), a quarterly forecasting panel drawn from member-bank economists, and a press/news stream. Additionally, the 'ČBA standard' quarterly disclosure format is what several banks in this cell (Partners Banka, Max banka) name for their capital-adequacy filings, so the association is also the format authority.
candidates.legal_status: trade-association publication; publisher copyright applies to commentary
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Track cbamonitor.cz sector pages plus the cbaonline.cz news and expert-output feeds (note pagination via limit/offset query parameters on /odborne-vystupy). Ingest the monthly banking statistics releases as a time series; use Hypomonitor for mortgage-channel context on MONETA, Raiffeisenbank and Partners Banka.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs-language trade-body query, derived from first-principles reasoning about who aggregates and benefits from sector data
queries_used: Česká bankovní asociace ČBA tiskové zprávy statistiky bankovní sektor cbaonline

candidates.source_name: Burza cenných papírů Praha (Prague Stock Exchange) – MONETA issuer detail & news
candidates.why_relevant: The exchange-side record for the cell's only listed bank: price and volume history, order book, market makers, a corporate calendar carrying shareholder meetings and financial-results announcement dates, dividend history with ex-date and record date, and a news tab carrying PSE and ČTK announcements. Useful as an independent confirmation of MONETA's reporting calendar and corporate actions, and as the market's real-time reaction signal to disclosures — a dimension no corporate source provides. Structured products written on MONETA shares are also listed here, an indirect indicator of retail interest.
candidates.source_subtype: stock exchange issuer page / market data
candidates.access_status: open web for the summary page; deeper historical market data may be licensed
candidates.legal_status: exchange publication; market data likely subject to redistribution licensing — collect metadata and calendar, not bulk tick data
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the issuer detail page by ISIN for the corporate calendar and dividend fields; subscribe to /novinky for exchange and ČTK announcements. Do not bulk-harvest price series without checking PSE redistribution terms.
candidates.discovered_via_method: surfaced by the cs seed query for MONETA results, then fetched to enumerate what the exchange publishes
queries_used: MONETA Money Bank vztahy s investory výsledky hospodaření prezentace

candidates.source_name: Patria.cz – regulated-information / issuer news feed (Czech financial wire)
candidates.why_relevant: Patria carries verbatim issuer regulated-information notices for Czech bond and equity issuers — the 'Banka CREDITAS a.s.: Výroční finanční zpráva za rok 2025' item is a filing notice, not journalism. This makes it a practical redundant path to filings from issuers whose own sites are bot-defended (CREDITAS returned 403 to a direct fetch) and a low-friction way to detect that a filing has occurred, with a timestamp. Numeric article ids make the archive enumerable.
candidates.source_subtype: financial newswire carrying issuer regulatory notices
candidates.access_status: open web; some Patria content is behind a client login
candidates.legal_status: publisher copyright on editorial content; the regulatory notices themselves are issuer-originated public disclosure
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Filter the /zpravodajstvi feed for issuer names in this cell plus filing keywords ('výroční finanční zpráva', 'pololetní finanční zpráva', 'vnitřní informace'); use hits as triggers to then fetch the primary document from the issuer or from the ČNB repository rather than relying on Patria's copy.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs-language search for a specific issuer's annual financial report surfaced a Patria filing notice; recognised as a wire/pointer and generalised
queries_used: Banka CREDITAS tiskové zprávy pro média výroční zpráva 2025 creditas.cz
Patria.cz zpravodajstvi regulované informace emitenti výroční finanční zpráva banka povinné uveřejnění

candidates.source_name: Czech retail-finance comparison & watchdog portals (Měšec.cz, Peníze.cz, Finparáda, Zlatá koruna, Banky.cz)
candidates.why_relevant: These portals systematically track exactly the disclosures this cell's banks make thinnest: fee-schedule changes, savings and term-deposit repricing, product launches, and structural events. Observed coverage in this session included Partners Banka's multi-currency account and in-app bitcoin offering, MONETA fee changes, the Max banka–CREDITAS merger mechanics and deposit-insurance consequences, Hello bank's wind-down, and CREDITAS's record 2025 profit — often with more operational detail than the banks' own releases. Peníze.cz additionally maintains a financial-subject database and a bank-ownership overview, useful for actor-map validation. Treat as corroboration and lead-generation, never as a primary citation.
candidates.source_subtype: consumer-finance trade press / product comparison aggregator
candidates.legal_status: publisher copyright — link-and-summarise only, no bulk republication
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Run keyword/entity alerts across these domains for each bank in the cell; use hits purely as triggers to go fetch the corresponding primary disclosure. Peníze.cz's financni-subjekty database and Finparáda's fee articles are worth periodic structured snapshots.
candidates.discovered_via_method: repeatedly surfaced across cs-language queries for every bank in the cell; consolidated into one aggregator-class entry
queries_used: Měšec.cz Finparáda Zlatá koruna srovnání bank poplatky novinky sledování bankovních produktů
Max banka fúze Banka CREDITAS 2025 sloučení zánik
Partners Banka tisková zpráva 2026 Max banka tiskové zprávy

candidates.source_name: Garanční systém finančního trhu – deposit guarantee scheme notices
candidates.why_relevant: The Czech deposit guarantee scheme publishes bank-specific notices at exactly the moments that matter structurally — mergers (its Creditas/Max banka page explains the combined EUR 100,000 limit and the three-month penalty-free withdrawal window), wind-downs and licence events. These notices are legally precise about effective dates, making them a better dating source for structural events than press coverage, and they identify which banks share a guarantee limit, which is itself an ownership-structure signal.
candidates.source_subtype: deposit guarantee scheme / statutory safety-net body
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-frequency crawl of the site's notice/news section; treat any new bank-specific page as a structural-event alert and cross-reference against JERRS and the ČNB disclosure-link list.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs-language merger query; recognised as a statutory safety-net publisher and retained as a structural-event source
queries_used: Max banka fúze Banka CREDITAS 2025 sloučení zánik

negative_findings.description: Max banka a.s. is named in this coverage cell as a live second-tier bank, but it is not one. Czech-language searching established that Max banka merged into its parent Banka CREDITAS, ceasing to exist as a separate legal entity with all contractual rights and obligations transferring to Banka CREDITAS; clients kept account numbers while the bank code moved from 4000 to 2250 with a transitional dual-code period. A direct fetch of maxbanka.eu confirmed the site now presents itself as the 'Max' product line of Banka CREDITAS, and its mandatory-disclosure archive stops at the FY2023 annual report and 30 September 2024 quarterly data. Reporting on the exact timing was not fully consistent across the sources found (the legal merger is reported as effective 1 October 2024, while Banka CREDITAS separately describes completing the Max banka integration during 2025), so the precise date should be confirmed against the Sbírka listin merger deed rather than press coverage.
negative_findings.result_summary: No live independent Max banka disclosure stream exists. maxbanka.eu remains reachable as a frozen historical archive (annual reports 2010–2023, ČBA-format quarterly filings 2021–Q3 2024) and should be harvested once, now, before decommissioning. Ongoing Max-related disclosure belongs to Banka CREDITAS.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Scheduling Max banka as a recurring source would produce a permanently stale, silently empty feed and would double-count or misattribute volumes that now sit inside Banka CREDITAS. It also means one of the ten named actors in this cell must be reallocated, and that CREDITAS's balance-sheet and client growth must be read as partly inorganic.

negative_findings.description: Hello bank! (operated in the Czech Republic by BNP Paribas Personal Finance SA, odštěpný závod, bank code 3050, Karla Engliše 3208/5, Prague 5) has exited the Czech market. Czech-language searching found that BNP Paribas Personal Finance announced a controlled wind-down of its Czech operations, stopped opening new accounts and offering further products from early April, sent contract terminations to clients, and provided payment accounts and consumer loans only until the end of November of that wind-down year; the stated rationale was that roughly 300,000 clients was below the scale needed to justify further investment against strong competition. A Komerční banka press release was also found recording an agreement to recommend a new contractual relationship to Hello bank's deposit clients. Searching specifically for a 2026 Hello bank Czech press centre returned no such thing.
negative_findings.result_summary: No live Hello bank Czech disclosure or press source exists to track. No Czech statutory annual report exists either, since the entity was an EU single-licence branch (odštěpný závod) rather than a Czech-licensed bank; it is absent from the ČNB list of bank mandatory-disclosure links.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Hello bank should be dropped from the live monitoring roster and retained only as a historical case study of challenger-bank exit economics in the Czech market. Its client migration is also a concrete competitive event for the surviving banks in this cell, and the Komerční banka arrangement means the beneficiary sits outside this cell in the top-four cell.

negative_findings.description: Both mBank (mBank S.A., organizační složka, IČO 27943445, Pernerova 691/42, Prague 8 – Karlín, operating in the Czech Republic since 2007) and the former Hello bank operate(d) as branches of EU-licensed banks under the single-licence / mutual-recognition regime, supervised primarily by their home regulator. Fetching the ČNB list of bank mandatory-disclosure links confirmed that neither mBank nor BNP Paribas / Hello bank appears among the roughly two dozen banks listed there.
negative_findings.result_summary: There is no Czech-law annual report, no local Pillar 3 filing and no local quarterly disclosure annex for mBank CZ. Its financials are only obtainable inside mBank S.A. Group reporting, where the Czech and Slovak branches are disclosed as a combined line within the Retail Banking segment — meaning Czech-only figures generally must be inferred rather than read off.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any cross-bank comparison table built from Czech statutory disclosures will silently omit mBank, understating challenger-segment share and distorting market-structure conclusions. Collection for mBank must be designed differently from the other eight actors — parent-group segment extraction plus the Czech press portal — and the CZ/SK aggregation must be flagged as a known precision limit rather than resolved.

negative_findings.description: The ČNB list designates https://www.airbank.cz/dokumenty-ke-stazeni as Air Bank's mandatory-disclosure location. Fetching that page returned only forms, contract documents, the price list, the interest-rate overview, business terms, complaint rules and privacy material. No links to annual reports (výroční zprávy), quarterly disclosure annexes or capital-adequacy data were visible on it, even though Air Bank's consolidated annual report PDFs demonstrably exist on the same host under a /file-download/ path.
negative_findings.result_summary: Air Bank's statutory annual reports are retrievable directly by path convention (/file-download/vyrocni-zprava-<YEAR>.pdf, with a numeric-prefixed variant observed for the newest edition) but are not discoverable by crawling the regulator-designated disclosure page. Quarterly and capital-adequacy annexes for Air Bank were not located in this pass at all.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collector that trusts the ČNB pointer and crawls only the designated page will conclude Air Bank publishes no annual report — a false negative on one of the cell's most strategically interesting challengers. It also means the regulator's pointer list resolves to a page rather than to a document index, and per-bank crawl rules must be written individually rather than generically.

negative_findings.description: Two priority sources resisted direct fetching in this pass. https://www.creditas.cz/povinne-uverejnovane-informace returned HTTP 403 Forbidden with no body, while individual PDFs on the same host surfaced normally through search — the signature of bot protection rather than absence. https://www.cnb.cz/cs/dohled-financni-trh/informace-zverejnovane-emitenty/ (the Central Repository of Regulated Information) ended in a socket hang up, while several sibling cnb.cz pages fetched successfully in the same session.
negative_findings.result_summary: Neither source is recorded as dead. Both are logged as blocked/unverified hypotheses with the observed blocker, and both were routed around: CREDITAS filings are reachable via /files/ document paths and via the Patria regulated-information feed, and the ČNB repository has documented sibling guidance pages that fetched successfully.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Recording either as dead on a single bad fetch would drop the cell's most active consolidator and the statutory single point of access for regulated information. It also sets the collection requirement: this cell needs a browser-grade fetcher with realistic headers, not a plain HTTP client, and needs redundant paths designed in from the start.

negative_findings.description: Across the eight domestically licensed banks in this cell, only MONETA Money Bank publishes a genuine quarterly earnings package (presentation, interim report, basic-data spreadsheet, press release, conference-call transcript, webcast video) with an investor calendar and sell-side coverage. Raiffeisenbank CZ produces a country-level investor presentation and half-year financial reports; Fio, Trinity Bank, Partners Banka and formerly Max banka publish only the ČNB/ČBA-format quarterly disclosure annexes, which are regulatory data tables with no narrative, no guidance and no management commentary. Air Bank publishes no local quarterly disclosure that was locatable in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Topic coverage for 'earnings' and 'investor relations' in this cell is structurally asymmetric: one issuer-grade stream, one partial, and the rest data-only. Narrative and forward-looking signal for the non-listed banks has to be reconstructed from press rooms, parent-group reporting and trade press.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Analytical expectations must be set accordingly — quarter-by-quarter competitive narrative is available only for MONETA and partly Raiffeisenbank, and any attempt to build a uniform quarterly comparison across the cell will either fail or silently over-weight the one bank that talks. It also means the annual report and press room carry disproportionate weight for six of the nine surviving actors.

negative_findings.description: Several actor names in this cell are seriously noisy in search and need disambiguation before automated collection. 'Partners' collides hard with Partners Group AG (the Swiss private-markets firm) and its SEC filings, and with 'Partners Group Private Equity' funds — an English-language query for Partners investor materials returned mostly Swiss results. 'Raiffeisen' returns Raiffeisen Bank entities in Serbia, Bosnia and elsewhere plus the Austrian parent, and within the Czech Republic alone spans Raiffeisenbank a.s., Raiffeisen investiční společnost, Raiffeisen stavební spořitelna and Raiffeisen – Leasing, each publishing its own výroční zpráva. 'Fio' spans Fio banka, Fio investiční společnost and the Fio brokerage news desk. 'mBank' spans the Polish parent, the Czech branch and the mbank.pl-hosted Czech media portal. 'Trinity' and 'Max' are common words that produce heavy false-positive volume without a bank qualifier.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bare-name queries are unusable for automated monitoring in this cell. Reliable retrieval required pairing each name with Czech disclosure vocabulary ('výroční zpráva', 'povinně uveřejňované informace', 'tisková zpráva') and, for the Raiffeisen and Partners families, with the exact legal form ('a.s.', 'Raiffeisenbank a.s.', 'Partners Banka a.s.').
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without name disambiguation rules and an IČO-anchored actor map, a monitoring pipeline for this cell will ingest Swiss private-equity filings as Czech banking intelligence and will conflate a bank with its sister investment company or building society. This is a design requirement for the collection layer, not a cosmetic issue.

coverage_gaps.description: Air Bank a.s. is one of the most strategically interesting challengers in the cell — PPF-owned, a repeated first mover on retail UX and pricing — yet this pass located only its consolidated annual report PDFs and its press room. No Air Bank quarterly ČNB/ČBA disclosure annex and no capital-adequacy filing was found, and the regulator-designated disclosure page does not link them. Its half-year position is visible only through PPF's 'Air Bank Group' combined results releases, which are unaudited and use a group perimeter that differs from the bank's own.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a targeted follow-up specifically for Air Bank quarterly disclosures using Czech regulatory vocabulary ('povinně uveřejňované informace k 30.6.', 'kapitálová přiměřenost', 'příloha 1'), probe /file-download/ for annex-style filenames, and fall back to the Sbírka listin filing for Air Bank a.s. (resolve its IČO via ARES first). Confirm whether the PPF 'Air Bank Group' perimeter includes Home Credit CZ/SK before using those numbers as bank figures.

coverage_gaps.description: Two of the ten actors named in this coverage cell are no longer live banks: Max banka merged into Banka CREDITAS and Hello bank wound down its Czech operations. That leaves eight live actors, of which one (mBank) has no Czech statutory disclosure at all. The cell rationale's premise — a long tail of licensed banks each carrying full statutory annual-report duties — holds for only six of the ten named entities.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Reissue the cell roster as: MONETA, Raiffeisenbank a.s., Air Bank, Fio banka, Banka CREDITAS (now including the Max product line), Trinity Bank, Partners Banka as Czech-licensed banks with full duties, plus mBank CZ as a single-licence branch requiring parent-group collection. Backfill the vacated slots from the ČNB disclosure-link list, which names roughly two dozen banks and therefore contains second-tier institutions not currently assigned to any cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Fetching the ČNB list of bank mandatory-disclosure links established that it covers roughly two dozen banks, materially more than the ten named in this cell plus the big four handled elsewhere. This pass did not enumerate and classify the remainder, so an unknown number of second-tier and specialist Czech-licensed banks (including building societies and specialist mortgage or corporate banks) currently have no scout assigned.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Do a mechanical full extraction of the ČNB list into a bank-to-disclosure-URL table, diff it against the union of all coverage cells in this run, and assign the residual banks to a follow-up cell. This is cheap, deterministic and closes the universe-boundary question for workstream A1 in a single pass.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell rationale specifically justifies a separate scout on the grounds that these banks disclose branch, ATM and digital-channel decisions that systemic banks bury. This pass found the channels where such news appears (each bank's press room, and Air Bank / Partners Banka releases that quantified mobile-app usage and client milestones) but did not locate any structured, comparable branch-count or ATM-network dataset per bank. ČNB ARAD and the payment-system statistics were identified as the likely home for aggregate channel data, but the specific series were not confirmed in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated follow-up on channel-footprint sources: identify the exact ARAD series ids for branch and payment-infrastructure counts, check whether ČNB supervisory statistics publish per-institution branch numbers, and evaluate ATM-network operators and the interbank ATM landscape as a separate source family. Also test whether each bank's annual report contains a consistent branch/ATM disclosure that could be extracted into a comparable series.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language coverage was achieved for every live actor: Czech-language queries were the ones that surfaced the ČNB disclosure-link list, the Fio quarterly XLSX annexes, the Trinity Bank archive, the Partners Banka document hub, the Max banka merger evidence, the Hello bank exit and the mBank Czech press portal — none of which reliably surfaced in English. The reverse gap is real though: English-language disclosure in this cell is thin and uneven. MONETA and Trinity Bank (2020 onward) publish English annual reports, Raiffeisenbank maintains an /en/ tree and an English investor presentation, and Partners Banka publishes English annual reports; Air Bank, Fio banka and Banka CREDITAS were not observed publishing English editions of their statutory reports in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat Czech as the mandatory primary collection language for this cell and English as an opportunistic parallel. For downstream analysis, budget for machine translation of Czech statutory PDFs rather than assuming English editions exist, and verify per-bank whether an English edition is a true translation or an abridged summary before treating the two as interchangeable.

coverage_gaps.description: Pointer and regulator-side sources were covered well (ČNB disclosure-link list, JERRS with its web services and open data, the Central Repository of Regulated Information, Sbírka listin, the national open-data catalogue). Independent third-party assessment sources were not: no credit-rating agency coverage of these banks was pulled beyond noting that MONETA maintains a ratings page, no auditor-identity mapping was compiled, and no ČNB supervisory enforcement or sanction record was searched. Job postings, procurement records and vendor case studies — which reveal payments and core-banking technology decisions indirectly — were not explored at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a follow-up pass on assessment and reveals-indirectly source families: rating-agency issuer pages for MONETA, Raiffeisenbank and Banka CREDITAS (a bond issuer); ČNB enforcement and sanction decisions; auditor identity per bank from the annual reports; and technology-vendor press releases, careers pages and public procurement mentions as indirect indicators of payments-platform investment.

coverage_gaps.description: Sources found in this pass disagreed on the timing of the Max banka absorption into Banka CREDITAS — press coverage placed the completed legal merger at 1 October 2024 with a transitional dual bank-code period, while CREDITAS's own 2025 results narrative described completing the Max banka integration during 2025. The maxbanka.eu archive is consistent with the earlier date (documents stop at FY2023 and Q3 2024) but does not state a merger date. Banka CREDITAS's acquisition of the Maltese MeDirect group was also identified as a major perimeter change affecting comparability, but its effective date and accounting treatment were not established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve both dates from primary records rather than press: pull the merger deed and the relevant annual report from Banka CREDITAS's Sbírka listin file, and check the ČNB JERRS as-of-date search to see when Max banka a.s. disappeared from the licensed-bank list. Flag FY2024 and FY2025 CREDITAS figures as perimeter-inconsistent until the MeDirect consolidation date is confirmed.

brief: The Czech second tier splits sharply into one issuer-grade disclosure machine and a long tail of statutory-minimum filers: MONETA Money Bank runs a full bilingual IR operation (quarterly presentations, transcripts, webcasts, XLSX data packs, IR calendar, sell-side previews from Fio's desk and a Prague Stock Exchange record), while Raiffeisenbank CZ sits in between with half-year reports, a country-level investor presentation and RBI group segment reporting behind it. Everyone else — Air Bank, Fio banka, Banka CREDITAS, Trinity Bank, Partners Banka — publishes annual reports plus ČNB/ČBA-format quarterly annexes and a press room, with Fio's and Trinity's .xlsx annexes and Partners Banka's superseded-document archive the most machine-friendly material in the cell; parent groups (PPF for Air Bank, mBank S.A. for the Czech branch, Partners Financial Services with its growth prospectus) carry the narrative the local entities omit. The regulator is the key that unlocks all of it: the ČNB list of bank mandatory-disclosure URLs resolves eight of the ten named actors in a single fetch, with JERRS, the Central Repository of Regulated Information and or.justice.cz Sbírka listin as the authoritative backstops. Two caveats dominate the cell — the roster is stale, since Max banka has merged into Banka CREDITAS (maxbanka.eu now a closing historical archive) and Hello bank has exited the Czech market entirely, while mBank as an EU single-licence branch files no Czech statutory report at all — and collection will need a browser-grade fetcher, as creditas.cz returned 403 and the ČNB repository dropped the connection, neither of which should be read as dead.
